_doc: Drive 9 round 3 face spec (d9_post.py; merged over wh2.json + faces_f2 'eyes_big' like r2_faces.json, which it replaces for round 3). Same stamp grammar (authored for a face turned toward +x: the near eye on the left with its outer corner at the left end; mirrored for -x). Legend: '.' keep, O lash (OL), a iris dark / top band (A2), c iris mid (A3), d iris light (A4), w catchlight (A5), W eye white (W2), K pupil (I4), k lash taper (I3), m brow (I2), 1-4 skin S1-S4. Round-2 face critic: 'eyes are oversaturated cyan discs with a thin lash line and no dark upper-lid mass; build the upper lid as a 2-3 px dark wedge with an outer flick, a dark pupil and a top shadow band on the iris, lower saturation; one face model across every shot; soften the n1/Q brows and mouths'. So: a lash wedge two rows deep (three with the flick), an A2 band under it, a 2x2 pupil, the catchlight on the same side in both eyes, a desaturated blue ramp; every shot takes the open eye (n1 and Q no longer use the lowered 'focus' or slanted 'fierce' lids), n1 a closed line mouth, Q a small symmetric open mouth; the stamp blush is off because r3_post draws its own; brows in a mid hair tone and none on a profile head.

idle_appeal.note: the knowing smirk (round-2 critic: lock the smirk as the default)

back_appeal.note: the same face turned: two eyes when the far eye faces the camera enough, else the profile eye

n1_contact.note: focused, not scowling: the open eye with a set mouth

q_stamp.note: the stamp's shout, small and symmetric
